text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bosnia's Council of Ministers on Tuesday agreed on immunity law but foreign trade policy was left unsettled due to concerns raised by Serb officials regarding special ties between the country's entities and Serbia and Croatia.

- Two Moslem houses were deliberately set on fire in the Croat-controlled region of Kupres in western Bosnia but perpetrators have not been found yet, local branch of the ruling Moslem Party of Democratic Action (SDA) says.
- Croat mayor of divided Bosnian town of Mostar Ivan Prskalo meets with a representative of Serb community in Mostar, Milan Bodiroga, to discuss problems of Serbs living there.

- Moslem deputy mayor of Mostar, Safet Orucevic, says that Mostar Moslems are ready to carry out all obligations given to them by the international community and adds that if the Croats are ready as well, Mostar's problems could be resolved quickly.

- Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) Media Experts Commission reafirms its committment to the protection of journalists working in Bosnia following recent reports of media harassment, OSCE spokesman says.

- Bosnian gas supplier "Energoinvest" threatens to cut off all gas supply orders for Bosnia from April 1, if Bosnian Serbs refuse again to pay their share of the outstanding debt to a Russian gas company or fail to attend international negotiations concerning this issue, the company says in a letter.

- Permanent Military Committee established at a session of Bosnia's collective presidency on Monday is a body which has to coordinate activities of all military forces in the country and to prevent mutual attacks, the daily says in a commentary.

- The United Nations Security Council in its presidential statement issued on Tuesday, strongly condemns the involvement of Bosnian Croat politicians in the February 10 incident in Mostar when one Moslem was killed and 22 wounded and asks for such incidents to be prevented in future.

- OSCE criticised Croat media in Mostar for unprofessional reporting of Moslem mayor's calls for Croat return to Moslem part of town, for inacurate reports on the local elections and misinterpretation of some OSCE officials. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
